The product rule for double summations states that

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{a}_{i}{b}_{j}={\sum }_{i=1}^{m}{a}_{i}{\sum }_{j=1}^{n}{b}_{j}.
$$

So, using the product rule for double summations, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{\sum }_{j=1}^{13}({a}_{i}-2)({b}_{j}-5) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{10}({a}_{i}-2){\sum }_{j=1}^{13}({b}_{j}-5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the rules for single summations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}({a}_{i}-2){\sum }_{j=1}^{13}({b}_{j}-5) & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{a}_{i}-{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}2)\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{13}{b}_{j}-{\sum }_{j=1}^{13}5) \\  & =({\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{a}_{i}-2{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}1)\cdot ({\sum }_{j=1}^{13}{b}_{j}-5{\sum }_{j=1}^{13}1) \\  & =(35-2\cdot 10)\cdot (70-5\cdot 13) \\  & =(35-20)\cdot (70-65) \\  & =(15)\cdot (5) \\  & =75.\end{aligned}
$$
